_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE CACHE-READING RULES ARE NOT VACUOUS — run it from
`reading.rs` pins these rules against TEXT rather than against the tree,
because the branches that matter are the ones this machine never takes. A
test over pinned text passes because the text is wrong as easily as because
the reader is right, so each injection below removes one reading rule and
names the test that must go red for it.
Scoped to this crate, not the workspace: these edits cannot reach a test
outside it, and the root suite is five minutes of proving nothing.
`red_set: exhaustive` — every red an injection raises is named, including
the ones it did not aim at. Until R1263 this manifest TOLERATED unnamed
reds, which is the weak claim R1140 made a format to replace: an injection
that turns four tests red while predicting one is an injection whose reach
nobody has read, and the number went 12 -> 34 in a single round without a
word being said about it. Naming them is what makes a red that MOVES a
failure rather than a smaller number.

injections.name: an-unknown-runner-is-guessed-at
injections.why: the key prefix is the identity every later comparison joins on, so a wrong `runner.os` reports every cache in the repository as missing — the loudest possible wrong answer, wearing the shape of a finding

injections.name: a-runner-is-resolved-for-every-job-not-every-caching-job
injections.why: one exotic uncached job would then make the whole workflow unreadable and the gate would report zero declarations — which reads as a tidy repository rather than as a reader that stopped

injections.name: the-whole-key-is-the-identity
injections.why: every key here ends in a `hashFiles` of the lockfiles, so a reader joining on the whole key calls every cache in the repository missing the day after a dependency bump

injections.name: only-a-saving-step-declares-a-cache
injections.why: a job that only restores still depends on that key surviving, which is the whole subject; reading `actions/cache` alone counts it as asking for nothing

injections.name: an-unreadable-hashfiles-argument-is-taken-as-a-glob
injections.why: the globs a key hashes are what excuses a cache this run had to rebuild; reading an expression like `env.LOCKS` as though it were a literal path would excuse a cold build that nothing justifies, and the strict direction is to excuse nothing

injections.name: needs-is-only-ever-a-list
injections.why: GitHub allows a single job id as well as a list, and a reader knowing only the list form answers "waits for nothing" for the single form — the same class of defect as reading `--flag value` but not `--flag=value`

injections.name: the-runners-name-for-the-workflow-is-taken-as-read
injections.why: R1107 — the reference is a JOIN KEY against the files this repository tracks, not a string to cut. A path nothing tracks compares unequal to every cache declaration's source, so `tools/cache-budget` would report every job in the repository as belonging to some other workflow — a verdict shaped like a reading with nothing behind it — and the census gate would load a file that is not there

injections.name: the-ref-is-cut-at-the-last-at-sign
injections.why: a branch name may hold anything a ref may hold, and the workflow path holds no `@` at all — so the first `@` ends the path and a reader taking the last one hands back a path with a ref glued to it, which then matches no tracked file and refuses a run that is fine

injections.name: the-repository-segments-are-not-skipped
injections.why: the reference begins `owner/repo/` and the path this repository tracks begins `.github/`; a reader that kept the head would answer with a spelling no tracked file has and refuse every run

injections.name: a-workflow-that-uploads-nothing-still-collects
injections.why: R1106's derivation, and R1107 leans on it from a second gate: a workflow uploading no artifact leaves nothing behind when its runners are destroyed, so a record written in it is unreadable by construction. A predicate that answered yes for every workflow would make the exemption cover the whole population and both gates would stop saying anything

injections.name: the-shallowest-manifest-match-wins
injections.why: `Cargo.toml` is itself a tracked manifest and is a suffix of every other one, so taking any match rather than the deepest reads every `--manifest-path bench/Cargo.toml` as the root workspace — and the root is one this repository pins, so a command over a workspace it CANNOT pin would be reported as compliant

injections.name: a-tail-under-a-variable-need-not-be-qualified
injections.why: `$ws/Cargo.toml` has a literal tail and it is `Cargo.toml`; without the qualification rule that resolves to the root workspace, and a gate pointed at a workspace chosen at runtime would be reported as pinning one it may never touch

injections.name: an-unmeasured-subcommand-is-assumed-harmless
injections.why: the whole law rests on knowing which subcommands rewrite a lockfile they disagree with; answering `leaves it alone` for one nobody has measured exempts it silently, which is the empty answer that reads like a clean one

injections.name: fmt-is-treated-as-a-resolve
injections.why: `cargo fmt` REJECTS `--locked`, so a law that required the flag of it is one no correct command can satisfy — and the gate would then demand a change that breaks every hook it touches

injections.name: a-free-resolve-over-an-owned-workspace-is-compliant
injections.why: this is the defect itself: a command that resolves without the flag rewrites the lockfile it disagrees with, so the check after it in the same run reads a repaired file. Calling it compliant is the state this repository was in for an unknown number of rounds

injections.name: the-flag-is-demanded-of-a-workspace-nobody-here-owns
injections.why: `studio` resolves against the sibling `pinion` checkout, so `--locked` there is a gate that turns red on a commit made in another repository — R1110's defect, which this law must forbid rather than merely permit

injections.name: a-command-behind-a-shell-keyword-is-not-a-command
injections.why: `if ! cargo test …` is how the git hooks write four of their five cargo invocations; a reader taking the first word literally answers `if` and leaves every one of them out of the population that the lockfile law walks

injections.name: every-word-in-front-of-cargo-is-skipped
injections.why: the mirror: skipping any leading word attributes `cargo test` to a line that runs some OTHER program with cargo as its argument, which puts a command nobody issues into the population and sends a later round fixing a flag on it

injections.name: the-build-machines-commands-are-not-this-repositorys
injections.why: R1197 — `[commands]` in the build-machine declaration is the fourth place a cargo command is written here, and while nothing read it all three were defective: none said `--locked`, so a lockfile disagreeing with the manifests was REWRITTEN by the machine that verifies this repository, and two of them ran a suite nothing judged for coverage. A reader that answers `no commands` puts them back outside every law and the finding disappears silently

injections.name: a-declared-command-does-not-say-which-one-it-is
injections.why: the role is what makes a finding actionable: this round's two gates printed `build`, `verify` and `sweep`, and a reader that recorded the FILE as the owner would print the same path three times and leave somebody to work out which of the three commands is the defective one

injections.name: a-wrapper-carries-no-command
injections.why: R1196, and this is the reading before it: a segment counted only when its FIRST word was `cargo`, so wrapping a suite in the script that judges what it covered DELETED that command from every population built on this crate — the largest `cargo test` in the tree would leave the gate that asks which tests CI runs, and the tests behind it would read as dark

injections.name: cargos-own-marker-starts-a-second-command
injections.why: the mirror of the hand-over rule: cargo's own bare `--` separates it from its harness, and a reader that treated it as a hand-over would go looking for a command inside `-- --nocapture` and find none — so `cargo test --workspace -- …` would vanish from the population entirely

injections.name: what-carried-the-command-is-thrown-away
injections.why: the wrapper's words are the only evidence that a run is judged for what it covered; discarding them leaves `cargo_args` identical for a wrapped and an unwrapped suite, and the law that every test run goes through the wrapper would have nothing to read

injections.name: an-unknown-ownership-verdict-is-read-as-owned
injections.why: the lister prints `ours` or `foreign`; a third word is a state nobody has written yet, and folding it into either answer decides the law for a case this reader has never seen

injections.name: every-declared-command-is-a-suite
injections.why: `unrun-tests` asks which tests each CI command executes; handing it the lint and citation commands as though they ran tests puts targets in its population that no command runs

injections.name: restore-keys-goes-back-to-being-unread
injections.why: R1116: the field that keeps two runs either side of a workflow edit comparable was DECLARED and read by nothing, so no measurement could contradict a sentence about it — and R1115 wrote the wrong sentence into the ledger

injections.name: a-fallback-that-still-hashes-is-accepted
injections.why: a `restore-keys` carrying the same expression as the primary key moves when it moves, so it falls back to nothing — the cold run one level down, wearing the shape of a fallback

injections.name: a-steps-own-bound-is-not-read-at-all
injections.why: R1237 — the datum the law over network fetches is built on. With this dropped, every step reads as one nobody bounded, and the law it feeds would report sixteen findings on a repository that had just repaired all of them. The direction that reads as good news is the other injection below

injections.name: a-steps-bound-is-taken-for-its-jobs
injections.why: and this is the direction that goes QUIET. Reading the step's own number as its job's makes every bound compare equal to itself, so `5 < 5` fails and `90 < 90` fails — but a repository whose steps are all bounded well under their jobs would go red for a reason that is not there, and one whose steps are bounded AT their jobs would agree with itself. A field read from the wrong node is not a smaller answer, it is a different question

injections.name: the-two-spellings-of-the-identity-need-not-agree
injections.why: THE QUIET ONE. A fallback that restores SOMETHING makes every job look warm while every gate here joins on a prefix GitHub is never asked for; both spellings read correctly alone, which is why only comparing them finds it

injections.name: a-jobs-budget-is-read-from-nowhere
injections.why: the quiet 360 minutes. A job with no `timeout-minutes` gets GitHub's own default, and a reader that finds none in a file that has them makes every job look like that — six hours a person can spend on somebody else's server before anything says so, and the file itself still reads as bounded

injections.name: a-jobs-shown-name-is-read-off-the-wrong-key
injections.why: the half that a join depends on. Every job in this repository declares the same `runs-on`, so a reader that takes its shown name from there gives every job one name — and a commit's answer, keyed on that name, then attributes one job's minutes to another. Reading a neighbouring key is the misread that looks least like one

injections.name: the-population-of-jobs-is-whatever-a-misspelling-finds
injections.why: a law over no jobs holds every job it found, which is what it would also do the day the `jobs:` key moved or a workflow stopped parsing. One letter is the whole distance between `every job is bounded` and `nothing was looked at`, and only a count says which one a green run means

injections.name: a-conditional-argument-is-read-as-a-certain-one
injections.why: R1262 — a flag added inside an `if` is neither present nor absent, and reading it as present is how a gate comes to say a command pins its lockfile when it pins it on some paths only. The reader answers `Sometimes`, and that answer is what keeps a `--locked` nobody can rely on out of the judged population

injections.name: a-bare-name-is-resolved-through-a-function-of-that-name
injections.why: R1262 — the first run's own defect. `Command::new(program)` inside a function TAKING `program` resolved through `fn program()` in the same file, and the one site that IS the door read as a second one. A call names a function; a bare name is a local or a parameter, and the two cannot share a map

injections.name: the-manifest-directory-becomes-a-runtime-value
injections.why: R1262 — `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` is decided by which crate the file belongs to, so a reader that knows the path knows the value. Left unread, three commands in this repository name no manifest at all and no law can say whose lockfile they resolve

injections.name: an-array-of-words-is-read-as-a-hole
injections.why: R1262 — an `.args([..])` has a KNOWN length even when its elements do not, and reading it as a hole throws away every flag written right there. Four of this repository's commands spell `--locked` inside such an array

injections.name: a-command-built-over-several-statements-loses-its-words
injections.why: R1262 — `let mut c = issue::cargo(..); c.arg(..)` is the same command as the same words in one chain, and a reader that followed only chains reports the tidier spelling as argument-free: a command with no `--locked` in it and nothing to notice

injections.name: the-door-is-recognised-only-when-its-module-is-spelled
injections.why: R1262 — `use ci_plan::issue::cargo;` and then `cargo(Tree::ThisRepository)` is the same door with one word less, and reading only the qualified path makes that command INVISIBLE rather than refused: the one direction this reader exists to rule out. No site in the tree is written that way today, which is exactly why the case is a fixture

injections.name: the-door-stops-being-recognised
injections.why: R1262 — every cargo command a Rust program issues comes through one door, and a reader that cannot see it sees no cargo commands at all: the declaration beside the words goes unread, and every site becomes something else

injections.name: a-call-inside-a-macro-is-not-looked-for
injections.why: `syn` hands macro invocations over as tokens and does not parse them, so `assert!(run(&[..]).is_ok())` is a call the walk cannot see. Left out, a wrapper whose other callers all wrote literals reads as one whose EVERY call site was read — the one way this hop can report a partly-read population as a whole one

injections.name: a-dotted-name-in-a-macro-is-read-as-a-free-call
injections.why: `x.run(..)` inside a macro is the receiver's `run`, and the only thing in the tokens that says so is the dot in front of it; without that the reader lists a call site that does not exist and leaves a site carried for a reason that is not true

injections.name: a-name-that-means-two-functions-is-followed-back-anyway
injections.why: a wrapper's words are read at its call sites, so a name two functions answer to hands one caller's literals to the other one's spawn — a cargo command in the population that nothing in this repository runs

injections.name: a-parameter-a-local-took-over-is-followed-back-anyway
injections.why: the name still reads like the parameter and is not it any more, so the call sites' literals would answer for words that never reach this spawn

injections.name: a-parameter-a-closure-took-over-is-followed-back-anyway
injections.why: the same shadowing one binding further in — a closure argument of that name is not the parameter, and reading it as one answers a question nobody asked

injections.name: a-call-qualified-by-a-type-counts-as-a-call-of-that-name
injections.why: `Command::new(..)` and `Path::new(..)` would become calls of whichever `fn new` is unique in the tree, and the words they hand over would be attributed to a wrapper that never took them

injections.name: an-associated-functions-parameters-are-followed-back
injections.why: an associated function is called `G::make(..)` and never bare, so a bare call of that name is somebody else's — an import, a macro's expansion. Following the parameter puts that caller's literals into a command nothing runs

injections.name: a-word-added-on-some-paths-is-filled-in-from-a-caller
injections.why: no caller's literal says whether a conditional flag is there, and a command reported as pinning a lockfile it pins every other Tuesday is the false green this reader exists to refuse

injections.name: the-callers-words-are-appended-rather-than-spliced
injections.why: a flag the wrapper adds after the caller's words would move in front of the subcommand; a command whose words were reordered is a different command, and every reading after it is about that one

injections.name: one-caller-read-is-taken-for-all-of-them
injections.why: a site four callers finished and a fifth did not is still a site with a hole; counting it as read is a partly-read population reported as a whole one, which is the shape R1190 named
